title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Okta (management API)
providers.scope_notes: Org authorization-server rules govern Okta APIs. Custom authorization-server lifetime policies do not govern these tokens.

controls.name: Token network restriction (API calls made with this token must originate from)
controls.what: Restricts where an SSWS token can be used from: any IP, or in/not in specific IP-based network zones.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Security > API > Tokens > Create token, or token > Security > Edit ('Token can be used from')
controls.quote: From the API calls made with this token must originate from dropdown list, select an option to specify where you allow connections to come from

controls.name: Admin role assignment (token inherits creator permissions)
controls.what: An SSWS token acts with the creating admin's current permissions, so limiting that admin's roles limits the token; only certain admin roles can create tokens.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Security > Administrators (roles of the creating user)
controls.quote: API tokens are generated with the permissions of the user that created the token. If a user's permissions change, then so do the token's. Super admins, org admins, group admins, group membership admins, and read-only admins may create tokens.

controls.name: Revoke token
controls.what: Admins can revoke any SSWS API token.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Security > API > Tokens > trash icon, or token page > Revoke token
controls.quote: On the API page Tokens tab, click the name of the token you want to revoke. On the token's page, click Revoke token .

controls.name: Deactivate token owner
controls.what: Deactivating the user who created a token makes Okta reject the token.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Directory > People > deactivate user
controls.quote: Tokens are valid only if the user who created them is active. Tokens issued by deactivated users are rejected.

controls.name: Token rate limits
controls.what: Caps the share of each API rate limit a single SSWS token can consume (default 50%).
controls.setting: Admin Console > Security > API > Tokens > token > Token rate limits > Edit
controls.quote: rate limits for token interactions are set automatically to 50 percent of each API maximum limit. See API rate limits . You can adjust this percentage for each token.

controls.name: Admin roles that can create API tokens (custom role needs Manage Users permission)
controls.what: Only super, org, group, group membership and read-only admins, or custom admin roles that include the Manage Users permission, can create SSWS tokens; other users cannot.
controls.setting: Admin role assignment / custom admin role permissions

no_control.what: Cannot change the 30-day idle expiry of SSWS tokens (no shorter or absolute lifetime).
no_control.quote: The 30-day period is fixed and can't be changed for your org.

no_control.what: Cannot use blocklist zones or non-IP zones to restrict SSWS tokens.
no_control.quote: You can only use IP-based zones with SSWS tokens. Ensure that you add them to the Gateway IP addresses field on the Add IP Zone page. See IP zones . You can't use blocklist zones with SSWS tokens.

controls_unknown: Whether any org-wide switch exists to disable SSWS token creation entirely (docs only show role-based limits on who can create tokens).
Whether network zones can restrict where OAuth service apps call Okta APIs from (org authorization server policies were not confirmed).
Default state of the Public client app admins setting.

authentication.summary: SSWS API tokens; scoped OAuth bearer. Service apps use client credentials authenticated with private_key_jwt.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Per-token IP/network-zone restrictions apply to SSWS API calls. Do not automatically extend that control to OAuth tokens.

lifetime.summary: 30 days unused; use resets clock; period fixed per org

renewal.summary: Each use extends the 30-day inactivity window. No refresh token is involved.

administration.summary: OAuth scopes plus assigned admin roles; SSWS inherits creator privileges. Revoke token or deactivate owner; token rate-limit allocation.
administration.conditions: Org authorization-server rules govern Okta APIs. Custom authorization-server lifetime policies do not govern these tokens.

offboard.details: Deactivating the creating user deprovisions all API tokens that user created.

inventory.details: Admin Console Security > API > Tokens tab lists tokens; GET /api/v1/api-tokens lists metadata of all active API tokens.

disable.ui: Security > Administrators: assign only roles that may create tokens (super/org/group/group membership/read-only admin); for custom roles, grant or withhold Manage API tokens

offboard.ui: Directory > People > More Actions > Deactivate > select creator > Deactivate Selected

token_format.notes: Sent as 'Authorization: SSWS <token>'. Doc example value starts with '00' but no format is documented. Token ID (not secret) looks like 00T... . Not in GitHub secret-scanning list.

log_sources.name: Okta System Log (Admin Console / GET /api/v1/logs)
log_sources.notes: Records admin/API actions with token or client context; 90-day retention; export to SIEM or Log Streaming for longer.

credential_id_fields.notes: Token ID of the SSWS token that caused the event; matches id in Security > API and /api/v1/api-tokens.
Admin user who owns the token; token inherits that user's privileges.
For SSWS requests, the ID of the agent making the request.

lifecycle_events.notes: Token changed (e.g. network condition); validity unchanged.
Request from outside the token's allowed network zone.

anomaly_cues: Token ID seen from an IP/ASN outside the integration's usual hosts
system.api_token.request_outside_allowed_range spikes (stolen token tried from attacker infra)
Browser user agent on events carrying requestApiTokenId
Token used for admin changes (role grants, MFA reset, new tokens) it never made before
system.api_token.create by an admin right after an unusual sign-in
Activity under a token whose owning admin was recently deactivated or had role removed

containment.steps: Revoke by ID: Security > API > Tokens, or DELETE /api/v1/api-tokens/{apiTokenId}. Deactivating the owning user deprovisions all their tokens. Add a network condition (PUT /api/v1/api-tokens/{apiTokenId}) to restrict use while investigating.
containment.notes: SSWS tokens are validated per request, so revocation stops use. Unused tokens expire after 30 days. Review what the token created (other tokens, OAuth apps, admin roles).

sample_query.purpose: All actions by one SSWS token from any IP other than the known integration host.

unknown: Dedicated event for invalid/failed SSWS token use (only outside-zone event found)
Whether every API-token event carries requestApiTokenId (read-only GETs may not be logged)

calls.reveals: Profile of the admin user who created the SSWS token (token owner, not a session user)
calls.log_notes: System Log does not record GET calls; token 'last used' in Admin Console still updates.

calls.reveals: Admin role assignments held by the token owner

calls.scope: okta.users.read (OAuth); SSWS inherits the owner's admin role
calls.log_notes: GET not in System Log; rate-limit dashboard can show top-consuming tokens.

calls.reveals: System Log events; lets the holder read the same telemetry defenders use (listLogEvents)

unknown: Per-endpoint rate limits for /users, /apps, /logs (bucket table not retrieved)
Whether any Okta add-on logs management-API reads
